hints: You may fix positions from left to right.
Find the value that belongs at the current position.
Reverse the segment from the current position to that value.
analogy: Bring the correct card to the front of the unsorted suffix by flipping that whole section.
example: For [3,1,2], reverse positions 1..2 to get [1,3,2], then reverse 2..3 to get [1,2,3].
algorithm: Store the permutation in an implicit balanced tree or implicit treap with lazy reversal. For i from 1 to n, find the current position j of value i, reverse the interval [i,j], and output that interval when j differs from i. Maintain parent pointers and subtree sizes, pushing lazy flags along the path before calculating a node?s index. At most n reversals are used.
correctness: Before step i, all positions before i are correct. Value i must lie at or after i. Reversing [i,j] places i at i without touching earlier positions, so induction fixes the whole permutation within n steps.
complexity: For n values, an implicit treap supports each index lookup and reversal in expected O(log n) time, for expected O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
